obtained.how: open-access PDF from the publisher (Frontiers in Plant Science)

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the article's first page
bibliography.note: Vilas, M. P., Marti, C. L., Adams, M. P., Oldham, C. E. & Hipsey, M. R. 2017. Front. Plant Sci. 8: 2097, published 08 December 2017, doi:10.3389/fpls.2017.02097; matches

claims.quote: varies seasonally from 1.2 m in spring to 0.3 m in autumn
claims.conditions: the lake's mean water depth; a eutrophic urban lake in Perth, Western Australia, 68.2 ha
claims.note: it is the mean depth that varies 0.3-1.2 m with season

claims.claim: beds filling more than half the water column stratified for about 8-12 h a day (modeled)
claims.quote: increased with canopy relative height, from 7.7 ± 2.9 h per day
claims.conditions: 3-D hydrodynamic model (ELCOM) fitted to the lake, canopy relative height 0.5 (7.7 ± 2.9 h/d) to 1 (12.3 ± 5.9 h/d), mean stratification duration; invasive Potamogeton crispus bed; no stratification below a relative height of 0.5

claims.claim: with gradients of up to 10 °C over 0.8 m
claims.quote: of 10°C between the water surface and sediment bed (0.8 m depth)
claims.conditions: measured (not modeled): maximum vertical temperature difference at the centre of the P. crispus bed, daytime, after 21 December 2014
claims.note: a field measurement; the sentence's '(modeled)' applies only to the hours of stratification

claims.claim: in the model a full canopy cut depth-averaged flow by about 90 %
claims.quote: depth-averaged water velocities within the macrophyte bed were only 0.001 m s−1
claims.conditions: ELCOM tracer runs for 28 January 2015, 10:00-20:00 h: 0.01 m/s (CV 25 %) with canopy relative height 0.1 against 0.001 m/s when the canopy reached the surface
claims.note: 1 − 0.001/0.01 = 90 % (project arithmetic). The comparison is with a 10 %-height canopy, not bare sediment.

claims.claim: canopy stratification needs plants filling at least half the water depth
claims.location: p. 6, Modeling results; abstract p. 1; field result p. 5
claims.quote: they occupied at least 50% of the water depth
claims.conditions: both field (stratification began once plants occupied more than 50 % of the depth) and model (threshold canopy relative height 0.5)
claims.note: the authors add that the threshold 'depends on other plant attributes such as the canopy density and biomass', on water transparency and on water depth, 'and so this threshold height may differ in other ecosystems' (p. 8); a fragmented bed (25 % cover) or a canopy without drag or light attenuation did not stratify in the model (p. 6). §3.4.7's application to low soft-water canopies is the project's inference.

notes: Other useful values: bottom DO at the bed centre ~18 mg/L by day and ~6 at night with short plants (November 2014); with stratification, anoxia at night (December) and before sunset (January 2015, 9 °C over 0.6 m); bottom redox to −450 mV during night anoxia. The paper proposes a plant-stratification-dieback feedback for the central die-off of the bed.
